title: Etale splitting of an integral morphism with finite fibre
statement: Let $\pi:T\to S$ be an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $s\in S$. Assume that $\pi^{-1}(s)$ is finite and that $\kappa(b)/\kappa(s)$ is finite-dimensional for every $b\in\pi^{-1}(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field] [def-pc-field-extension]. There exist an affine scheme $U$, an etale morphism $g:U\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a point $u\in U$ with $g(u)=s$, an integer $m\geq0$, and pairwise disjoint open-and-closed affine subschemes $V_1,\ldots,V_m$ whose union is $T\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product], such that each $V_i\to U$ is integral and has exactly one point $v_i$ over $u$, and $\kappa(v_i)/\kappa(u)$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. The integer $m$ need not equal the number of points of $\pi^{-1}(s)$ before base change; if $m=0$, the union is empty.

proof.text: Enumerate the finitely many points of $T$ over $s$, without repetition. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-split-residue-points] to these points and $\pi$: its finite-residue-extension hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis here. It gives an etale neighbourhood $(U_0,u_0)\to(S,s)$ for which the whole fibre of $T_0=T\times_SU_0$ consists of finitely many distinct points $z_1,\ldots,z_m$, each with finite purely inseparable residue extension over $\kappa(u_0)$. The lists over different original points cannot overlap because the first projection has different values. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink] with the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u_0)\to U_0$ and $W=U_0$, to replace $U_0$ by an affine open containing $u_0$. This does not change this fibre or its residue fields. The same construction allows $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 02LM, label lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-multiple-points-var, proof: residue-field splitting; affine shrinking by Tag 04HX, label lemma-describe-etale-local-ring

proof.text: Write $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$, let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ correspond to $u_0$, and put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] write $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-sbc-integral-morphism-base-change] and [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $A\to B$ is integral. Its fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}F$ with $F=B\otimes_Ak=(A\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}(B/\mathfrak pB)$; its points are exactly the $z_i$, by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, localization at $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and quotient by $\mathfrak p$ do not change the residue field: the resulting residue field is $\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, with the same map from $k$. Thus the residue extensions from step 1 are also the residue extensions of these fibre points. A further base change to $k$ is integral, so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal] says every prime of $F$ is maximal. Consequently every point is closed; a finite space with every point closed is discrete, since the complement of any singleton is a finite union of closed singletons. No finite-type or Artinian hypothesis on $F$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, label lemma-etale-makes-integral-split, second proof, first paragraph; Tag 01WL, label lemma-base-change-finite; Tag 00GS, label lemma-integral-over-field

proof.text: For each singleton $\{z_i\}\subset\operatorname{Spec}F$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] supplies an idempotent $\delta_i\in F$ with $D(\delta_i)=\{z_i\}$. These are orthogonal: for $i\ne j$, the idempotent $\delta_i\delta_j$ has empty basic open, so uniqueness in that same correspondence makes it zero. Their sum is idempotent and has basic open the whole spectrum (at each prime exactly one summand is $1$), so the sum is $1$ by uniqueness. If $m=0$, the empty sum is $1$ in $F$: indeed the same correspondence identifies the idempotents $0$ and $1$ when the spectrum is empty. Thus this construction does not require $F$ reduced or Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00EE, label lemma-disjoint-decomposition; used as the product-decomposition input in the second proof of Tag 0BSR

proof.text: Descend these finitely many idempotents from $F$ to a quotient before lifting them. Express each $\delta_i$ as $b_i/a_i$ in $(A\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}(B/\mathfrak pB)$, where $a_i\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$. First invert the product of the $a_i$. In the resulting localization of $B/\mathfrak pB$, each of the finitely many errors $\delta_i^2-\delta_i$, $\delta_i\delta_j$ ($i\ne j$), and $\sum_i\delta_i-1$ maps to zero in $F$. For each error $x$, the definition of equality in a localization gives $c_x\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $c_xx=0$. Invert also their product. With $h=(\prod_i a_i)(\prod_x c_x)\notin\mathfrak p$, all these equations hold in $B_h/\mathfrak pB_h$. The basic open $D(h)$ contains $u_0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink] with $W=D(h)$ to obtain an affine open $U_1=\operatorname{Spec}A_1$ containing $u_0$, lying inside $D(h)$, and etale over $S$. The element $h$ is invertible on $U_1$, so $A\to A_1$ factors through $A_h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] its pulled-back coordinate ring is $B_1=B\otimes_AA_1$. Map the constructed idempotents from $B_h/\mathfrak pB_h$ to $B_1/\mathfrak p_1B_1$, where $\mathfrak p_1$ is the prime of the retained point. This quotient map is defined because every element of the old $\mathfrak p$ maps into $\mathfrak p_1$. Since $U_1$ is an open subscheme containing $u_0$, its local ring at that point, and hence its residue field, is unchanged. Consequently $B_1\otimes_{A_1}\kappa(\mathfrak p_1)\cong B\otimes_Ak=F$, and the mapped family restricts to the same $\delta_i$. Rename these rings $A,B$ and the point $\mathfrak p$. We have a complete orthogonal family $\bar\delta_i\in B/\mathfrak pB$ mapping to the original $\delta_i$. For $m=0$ there is only the error $-1$, and the same annihilator argument applies. The point and its fibre are retained because every inverted element is outside $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, label lemma-etale-makes-integral-split, second proof, finite-equation descent of idempotents; denominator descent supplied explicitly by the agent; basic-open coordinates Tag 01I3, label lemma-standard-open-affine

proof.text: Lift the family by a finite induction using [lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotent-upstairs]. Set $A_0=A$, $B_0=B$. The induction hypothesis after $r$ steps is: $A\to A_r$ is etale, the canonical map $A/\mathfrak p\to A_r/\mathfrak pA_r$ is an isomorphism, $B_r=B\otimes_AA_r$ is integral over $A_r$, and the first $r$ quotient idempotents have lifts $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in B_r$. For the next step apply that node to $A_r\to B_r$, the ideal $I_r=\mathfrak pA_r$, and the image of $\bar\delta_{r+1}$ in $B_r/I_rB_r$. This quotient is canonically $B/\mathfrak pB$ because $A_r/I_r\cong A/\mathfrak p$. The node gives an etale map $A_r\to A_{r+1}$ inducing an isomorphism on the quotients, and the required next lift; pull back the previous lifts. Integrality at the next stage follows from [lem-sbc-integral-morphism-base-change]; etaleness of the composite follows from clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-localization-functor-adjoint]. After $m$ steps put $A_*=A_m$, $B_*=B\otimes_AA_*$. The ideal $\mathfrak p_*=\mathfrak pA_*$ is prime because $A_*/\mathfrak p_*\cong A/\mathfrak p$ is a domain. It lies over $\mathfrak p$, and this isomorphism induces $\kappa(\mathfrak p_*)\cong k$. Hence the fibre ring at $\mathfrak p_*$ is canonically $F$ and the $f_i$ restrict to $\delta_i$. The base case $m=0$ is the identity extension, with no lifts to choose.

source.place: Tag 07M4, label lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs; finite-family induction and quotient identifications written explicitly by the agent

proof.text: The lifts need not be mutually orthogonal. Define $e_i=f_i\prod_{j<i}(1-f_j)$ in the commutative ring $B_*$, and $e_\infty=\prod_{j=1}^m(1-f_j)$. Products of commuting idempotents are idempotent. If $i<j$, then $e_ie_j$ contains $f_i(1-f_i)=0$. Writing $P_0=1$ and $P_i=\prod_{j=1}^i(1-f_j)$ gives $e_i=P_{i-1}-P_i$; summing cancels every intermediate $P_i$. The telescoping identity $\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\prod_{j<i}(1-f_j)+\prod_{j=1}^m(1-f_j)=1$ shows completeness. Restriction to $F$ sends $e_i$ to $\delta_i$, since the $\delta_i$ are orthogonal, and sends $e_\infty$ to $0$. This includes the empty family, where $e_\infty=1$ and $F$ is the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 07M4, label lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs, applied finitely many times; elementary orthogonalization and telescoping identity supplied by the agent

proof.text: Put $V_i=D(e_i)$ and $W=D(e_\infty)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B_*$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] they are open and closed, and by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] they are affine. The equations in the preceding step make them pairwise disjoint and covering: in any residue field an idempotent is $0$ or $1$, orthogonality allows at most one of the $e_i,e_\infty$ to be $1$, and their sum forces one to be $1$. For an idempotent $e$, its localization ring $B_*[1/e]$ is $B_*/(1-e)$: after $e$ becomes invertible the relation $e^2=e$ makes $e=1$, and conversely imposing $e=1$ inverts it. Every element of this quotient satisfies the monic equation satisfied by a representative in $B_*$. Thus each $V_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_*$ and $W\to\operatorname{Spec}A_*$ is integral, by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The fibre of $V_i$ at $\mathfrak p_*$ is $D(\delta_i)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}F$, hence consists of the one point $z_i$ with the purely inseparable residue extension established in step 1; the fibre of $W$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 00EE, label lemma-disjoint-decomposition; affine basic opens Tag 01I3, label lemma-standard-open-affine; quotient integrality verified directly

proof.text: Remove the remainder on the base. Since $W\to\operatorname{Spec}A_*$ is integral, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-spec-closed-map] makes its image closed. That image misses $\mathfrak p_*$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] choose $t\in A_*\setminus\mathfrak p_*$ with $D(t)$ disjoint from the image. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink] to the etale map $\operatorname{Spec}A_*\to S$, the canonical residue-field point at $\mathfrak p_*$, and the open $D(t)$. It gives an affine open $U\subseteq D(t)$ containing the marked point whose composite to $S$ is etale. Replace every $V_i$ by its pullback to $U$. There is now no remainder, since a point of its pullback would map into both $D(t)$ and the image of $W$. The $V_i$ stay affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and integral by [lem-sbc-integral-morphism-base-change]. They remain disjoint open-and-closed subschemes, cover $T\times_SU$, and retain their single fibre points and residue fields at the unchanged marked point $u$. This proves every clause. If $m=0$, $W$ was the whole pullback before shrinking and its removal leaves $T\times_SU=\varnothing$.
